subject.title: fix(sessions): keep gateway responsive while large transcript archives are built

question: After a rebase onto current main, should maintainers accept this bounded worker-based Phase 1 while the linked issue retains streaming extraction and chunked reclamation as separate work?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes the execution boundary for durable persisted-session cleanup and intentionally leaves some synchronous reclamation and whole-buffer memory behavior for later phases; deciding that staged tradeoff is product and operational ownership judgment.

options.title: Merge Phase 1 after refreshed proof
options.body: Accept the bounded event-loop responsiveness improvement after the rebased archive-worker, lifecycle-race, packaging, and built-gateway proof remains green.

options.title: Require full streaming in this PR
options.body: Hold the change until it also bounds archive-generation memory, at the cost of combining a substantially larger persistence redesign into this worker migration.

options.title: Keep the existing synchronous path
options.body: Decline the staged worker approach if the remaining whole-buffer archive cost is not acceptable for the supported gateway lifecycle contract.

recommendation.title: Merge Phase 1 after refreshed proof
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded event-loop responsiveness improvement after the rebased archive-worker, lifecycle-race, packaging, and built-gateway proof remains green.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the adjacent archive durability boundary that this PR extends into worker execution.
